name: Connecticut
rule: Owed in the form of wages if the employer policy or union contract provides payment of accrued fringe benefits on termination.

name: Illinois
rule: Earned vacation is final compensation, paid by the next regular payday; a policy may not forfeit earned vacation at separation.

name: Iowa
rule: Owed only where an agreement or policy provides it; pro rata if the policy accrues pro rata.

name: Maine
rule: Unused paid vacation accrued on and after January 1, 2023 is paid at separation, unless the employer has 10 or fewer employees or is public (a union contract can override).

name: Maryland
rule: Accrued leave is paid at termination unless a written policy limits it, the employee was told of the leave benefits, and the policy denies payment.

name: North Dakota
rule: Accrued PTO is paid at separation; on a voluntary quit a private employer may withhold it only with written notice at hiring, under one year of service and under five days' notice.

name: Oklahoma
rule: A written policy promising payout makes vacation wages.

name: Oregon
rule: No legal requirement; an established policy or agreement on accrued vacation must be honored at termination.

name: South Carolina
rule: Wages include vacation, holiday and sick leave payments due under an employer policy or contract.

name: South Dakota
rule: No law requires paid leave; it is a matter of employer policy.

name: Tennessee
rule: Only if the employer's policy or labor agreement requires it.

name: Texas
rule: Vacation and sick leave pay are wages only when owed under a written agreement or written policy.

name: Vermont
rule: Not required, but written agreements (a handbook counts) providing vacation make the employer liable for it.

name: West Virginia
rule: Fringe benefits payable under a written policy are part of final wages unless the policy sets a later date.

name: Wyoming
rule: Payout can be denied only if a written policy clearly says so and the employee acknowledged it.
